title: Pesto Beans
description:
By Christian Reynoso in the NYT: Part quick and rustic bean stew and part deconstructed pesto, this pesto-inspired one-pan meal requires no blender and minimal slicing. It all starts out by sizzling nuts with a little turmeric in olive oil until golden. The Parmesan cheese makes a creamy base for softened shallots and tender beans; then freshly torn basil leaves and lemon juice are stirred in at the end so they stay vibrant and fresh. Top with the beautifully toasted nuts, golden olive oil and a bit more Parmesan. Serve with crusty bread or garlic bread on the side.
You might also serve this with some simply grilled Italian sausages, regular or hot; or maybe some Italian meatballs which you could add into the pesto bean sauce for a minute or two before serving.
ingredients: ¼ cup pine nuts or sliced almonds
2 (15.5-ounce) cans cannellini beans or other creamy white beans, drained
1 cup finely grated Parmesan (about 4 ounces), plus more for serving
1 lemon, cut into wedges, for serving
directions: Heat 6 tablespoons of the olive oil over medium-low in a 12-inch skillet or small Dutch oven. Add the pine nuts and, when the oil starts sizzling, stir occasionally until golden brown, about 5 minutes; turn off heat. Stir in the turmeric and season lightly with salt and pepper. Transfer to a small serving bowl.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium-high in the same skillet. When warm, add the shallots and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring until just softened, about 3 minutes. Stir in the garlic, and when sizzling (about 1 minute), stir in the beans and stock. Bring to a simmer then turn heat down to low.

A little at a time, sprinkle in the cheese, stirring vigorously to combine. When the cheese has melted into the broth and the mixture looks creamy, season to taste with salt and then turn off the heat. While the beans are still hot, tear the basil leaves (or roughly chop, if you prefer) and stir into the beans.
Serve hot, in bowls or on plates, drizzled with the sizzled nuts and some (or all) of the nut oil, a squeeze of lemon juice and more black pepper and grated Parmesan, if desired.
